gloss: tottering; staggering; unsteady on one's feet

definitions.explanation: Describes a wobbling, unstable walk — as of a toddler, an elderly person, a drunk, or someone too exhausted to keep their balance. More emphatic than よろよろ, often suggesting a precarious, almost-falling gait.

examples.japanese: よたよた⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{歩|ある}いた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧よたよた⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{歩|ある}き→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
⟦{疲|つか}れ→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧⟦{切|き}って→切る：02693_kiru⟧、よたよたし⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{帰|かえ}った→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: Exhausted, I made my way back to the station, staggering.

notes:
Mimetic of unsteady walking. Used adverbially with ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧ or by itself; also combines with ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ as よたよた⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to walk unsteadily).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- よたよた⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧: to walk unsteadily
- よたよた⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be unsteady on one's feet
- よたよた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{足取|あしど}り→足取り：10625_ashidori⟧: a wobbly, staggering gait

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦よろよろ→よろよろ：05368_yoroyoro⟧: tottering — similar but slightly less dramatic; suggests swaying
- ⟦ふらふら→ふらふら：05367_furafura⟧: woozy; staggering — emphasizes dizziness rather than weakness
- ヨボヨボ: feeble; decrepit — of old age, more about general frailty than a walk
